newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK C.BANK HEAD SAYS STABILITY A MUST FOR ECONOMY.
newsitem.headline: TURK C.BANK HEAD SAYS STABILITY A MUST FOR ECONOMY.

text.p: Turkish central bank governor Gazi Ercel said Turkey's economic development was encouraging but stability and longer term targeting were needed for further improvement.

"I see Turkish economic developments encouraging, but Turkey should provide economic and political stability and must have longer term projections rather than short-term," Ercel told a two-day Euromoney conference which started on May 14.
"To realise this, a continuing growth and lower inflation is needed," Ercel added.
Ercel said Turkey would face many problems in the integration process with European Union (EU), but it also had opportunities ahead and should benefit from them.
"There will be some difficulties in the integration with the EU, but Turkey should know to how benefit from all the developments," he added.
Ercel said Turkey's main economic weakness were high inflation, which was at 77.2 percent year-on-year in April, and budget deficits, which were 1,217 trillion lira for 1996.
But he said Turkey's "dynamism and openness" would help overcome such problems.
"High inflation and budget deficits are our weakness but on the other hand Turkish economy is very dynamic," he added.
Turkey's domestic debt stock grew by 131.4 percent to 3,149 trillion lira in 1996, fuelling inflation and public deficits.
Debt stock stood at 3,834 trillion lira at end-March, from a 3,604 trillion lira previous month.

Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said earlier this week the budget, targeted to be balanced in 1997, gave a deficit of more than $1 billion in March. --Tulin Aygunes, Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
